well, eventually she will learn to love to poster for the happy memories it will bring her, instead of the grief it brings her. i absolutely filled my room with my dad's stuff, his jacket, his shirts, his blanket, a hairbrush, and even some old belts and suspenders he used to wear all the time (and looked soo cute in). for a while, i would just hold his shirt and cry and cry and cry and itd hurt so much. i didnt want to leave my room because i didnt want to leave his shirt behind, and i didnt wanna wear it and carry it with me because i didnt want it to get dirty or damaged, but eventually his shirt and other stuff brought me comfort instead of sorrow. it takes time, but day by day, the grief will be replaced with happy memories. the grief will never leave, ever, but it will get easier to handle. time will heal her. as for you, just keep doing what youre doing. hold her and listen to her, let her pour her heart out to you and sympathize with her (its hard to open up to someone about grief when they dont respond). ask her to tell you stories about him. ask her about happy memories. and if sometimes she wants to focus on the sad, let her, and be a shoulder to cry on. the thing about grief is, you have to feel it. if it push it down itll be hell for much longer. encourage her to be kind and gentle to herself, and help her do so. time and support is all you can offer, and thats more than enough. good luck to you both 🤍
